summary: Ten concrete, comment-endorsed tools and media picks from a verified 30-story HN front-page crawl.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Treedix USB Cable Tester
items.source_story_title: I stopped trusting USB-C cable labels and started testing them
items.summary: A cable tester for sorting USB cables by wiring and finding broken ones.
items.why_included: A first-hand user called it awesome after checking every cable they owned.
items.evidence: A commenter said the tester exposed a cable with only its ground connected, which they immediately discarded.

evidence_sources.author: lrasinen
evidence_sources.excerpt: The Treedix cable tester is awesome.

items.name: nano-vLLM
items.source_story_title: Inside vLLM: Anatomy of a High-Throughput LLM Inference System (2025)
items.summary: A compact vLLM implementation for learning the essentials of fast LLM inference.
items.why_included: It was singled out as a more approachable route to understanding a complex inference stack.
items.evidence: A commenter recommended reading its roughly 5,000 lines because it retains the major pieces that make an inference engine fast.

evidence_sources.author: miki123211
evidence_sources.excerpt: Another great way to understand how vllm works is to read the code of nano-vllm

items.name: Wyzer
items.summary: An experimental language that treats distributed communication as a choreographed program.
items.why_included: Its attempt to generalize server-function style coordination into a language feature drew a concrete endorsement.
items.evidence: A commenter described its choreography feature as a generalized form of server functions and called it a cool idea.

items.name: textlog
items.source_story_title: Show HN: textlog – A quiet, text-only microblogging platform, open-source, no JS
items.summary: A no-JavaScript, open-source microblog built around individual short notes rather than blogs.
items.why_included: Its note-first model was praised as lowering the psychological friction of posting.
items.evidence: A commenter called it neat and said individual notes make quick posting easier than managing a blog identity.

items.name: qxw
items.summary: An open-source crossword constructor with grid filling and unusual grid topologies.
items.why_included: It is a direct recommendation for anyone inspired to experiment with nonstandard crosswords.
items.evidence: A commenter called qxw a wonderful open-source app for making crosswords with interesting topologies.

evidence_sources.author: zem
evidence_sources.excerpt: is a wonderful open source app that lets you make crosswords with interesting topologies, complete with grid filler support, if anyone wants to experiment with them.

items.name: Prime Quine ASIC
items.source_story_title: A quine in Piet – a GIF image that prints itself [video]
items.summary: A self-reproducing ASIC that displays its own Verilog source over VGA.
items.why_included: It is a delightfully concrete hardware quine with both source and a browser-viewable simulation.
items.evidence: Its creator surfaced it specifically to readers interested in visual-output quines.

evidence_sources.author: jamesaross
evidence_sources.excerpt: If you like quines with a visual output like this, I recently taped out an self-reproducing ASIC

items.name: The Storm Before the Storm
items.source_story_title: US strikes $1.2B deal to pay German firm to halt offshore wind projects
items.summary: Mike Duncan's history of the Roman Republic's destabilization before its final collapse.
items.why_included: A commenter recommended it as a useful account of the forces that set Rome's republican decline in motion.
items.evidence: A commenter said it covers what set the fall of the Republic in motion and praised Duncan's related History of Rome narration.

evidence_sources.author: hnra
evidence_sources.excerpt: covers what sets in motion the fall of the republic.

items.name: The Salt of the Earth
items.source_story_title: São Paulo resident transforms degraded area into urban forest
items.summary: A documentary about photographer Sebastião Salgado's work and changing landscapes around the world.
items.why_included: It was directly recommended in a thread about one person's long-running urban reforestation effort.
items.evidence: A commenter explicitly recommended Sebastião Salgado's documentary, The Salt of the Earth.

evidence_sources.author: rbreve
evidence_sources.excerpt: Related a recommend this documentary by Sebastião Salgado, The Salt of the Earth

items.name: The Man Who Planted Trees
items.source_story_title: São Paulo resident transforms degraded area into urban forest
items.summary: Frédéric Back's animated short about a shepherd patiently restoring a barren valley.
items.why_included: It is an apt, concrete viewing recommendation for a discussion of persistent individual ecological repair.
items.evidence: A commenter shared the film directly in response to the urban-forest story.

items.name: Petri Nets as a Music Sequencer
items.source_story_title: Petri Nets as a Music Sequencer
items.summary: A visual rhythm sequencer exploring Petri-net and rhythm-necklace representations.
items.why_included: A practicing commenter found the representation a strong balance of simplicity and expressive rhythmic detail.
items.evidence: A commenter described the approach as a very nice balance of simplicity and expressiveness for swing, microtiming, and groove.

evidence_sources.author: jarth9
evidence_sources.excerpt: Compared to other ways of writing down musical rhythm, I've found this to be a very nice balance of simplicity and expressiveness.
